blocks.text: St. Conleth, also called Conláed, was the first bishop of Kildare. The historical reference traces his early life to a hermitage near the River Liffey and attributes this account to the early Life of St. Brigid by Cogitosus.
blocks.reason: Concise, source-bound biographical teaching; source wording and later received traditions are distinguished from canonical Scripture.

blocks.text: According to that Life, St. Brigid invited him to exercise episcopal ministry in her double monastery, a community including women and men. He shared in its governance. Irish genealogical traditions also describe him as a skilled metalworker. These details belong to identified medieval sources; the later claims about the reach of Kildare’s authority require their own historical context.
blocks.reason: Concise, source-bound biographical teaching; source wording and later received traditions are distinguished from canonical Scripture.

sections.title: Death and limits of the evidence

blocks.text: The records place his death in either 516 or 520. A later story says that wolves killed him during a journey; the reference notes that this may be a legend connected with an explanation of his name. It should not be reported as an independently established martyrdom.
